body.statement:
Under the frozen definition of \(\mathfrak L_U(P_0)\), the requested uniform asymptotic-linear conclusion, and hence the requested four-part affirmative attainment result, is false in general. Specifically, take \(P_0=P^{\star}\) and fixed constants for which \(P^{\star}\) has strict slack in every support, fourth-moment, SC-rank, positive-normal-eigenvalue, and local-score-variance inequality entering \(\mathfrak L_U(P^{\star})\), and for which the displayed Gram rank is locally constant. For every sufficiently small nonzero \(\delta\), let \(Q_\delta\) retain the donor means and innovation laws of \(P^{\star}\) but replace the treated untreated mean path by \((-2\delta,-4\delta,-4\delta)\), and define
\[
 \Delta_\delta
 =\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(Q_\delta;\mathrm{PT},P^{\star})
  -\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(Q_\delta;\mathrm{SC},P^{\star}).
\]
Then \(Q_\delta\in\mathcal M_I\) and
\[
 E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta^2]\ge\frac{15}{2}\delta^2>0.
\]
For every sample size, finite-coordinate splicing produces two elements of \(\mathfrak L_U(P^{\star})\) having the same observed law at that coordinate but different admissible chart labels. No single estimator can have both chart expansions uniformly. This obstruction proves no affirmative sequencewise continuation theorem; it merely does not rule out such a theorem after imposing a common local neighborhood, common bounds on the QMD scores and remainders, and exclusion of arbitrary finite-coordinate replacements.
body.justification: At a witness admitted with strict slack, the off-intersection chart definitions include branch-specific composition gradients; in the one-stratum construction both vanish, leaving the quantitative separation and finite-coordinate-splicing contradiction unchanged.
body.gap: The integrated estimator's branch-specific asymptotic laws and generic multiplier results do not validate uniformity over a class closed under arbitrary finite-coordinate replacement, even around a strict-interior center.
body.consumer: Applied users should treat the envelope as a strict-interior lower-bound benchmark; a branch-robust confidence interval requires a redesigned uniformity class and a new positive theorem.
body.proof_tex:
Choose the fixed constants so that \(P^{\star}\) satisfies every inequality defining the local class with strict slack and its finite Gram rank is locally constant. This choice is possible by \(\mathrm{prop{:}strict\text{-}three\text{-}group\text{-}witness}\); moreover \(V_U(P^{\star})=39/4>\kappa_0\) because \(\kappa_0<1\), giving strict local-score variance slack at the center.

For sufficiently small fixed \(\delta\ne0\), retain both donor mean paths and all innovation laws, but replace the treated untreated mean path by
\[
 (1/2+\delta)(-1,-2,-2)+(1/2-\delta)(1,2,2)
 =(-2\delta,-4\delta,-4\delta).
 \tag{1}
\]
Give the treated group the same additive final treatment effect and call the law \(Q_\delta\). Every untreated final mean change remains zero, so PT holds. The donor matrix is unchanged, and the treated path is reproduced by the unique weights
\[
 w_\delta=(1/2+\delta,1/2-\delta)^{\prime},
 \tag{2}
\]
so SC holds as well. The strict inequalities and constant rank persist for all sufficiently small \(|\delta|\) by continuity of the finite cell moments, singular values, Gram eigenvalues, and chart variances. Thus \(Q_\delta\in\mathcal M_I\) and it obeys every fixed local-class margin.

There is one covariate stratum. On either branch \(C_b(X)=\theta_b\) is constant, hence
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{PT}}(Q_\delta)=\chi_{\mathrm{SC}}(Q_\delta)=0.
 \tag{3}
\]
Thus the branch-specific composition terms in \(\mathrm{def{:}local\text{-}score\text{-}extension}\) cancel in the chart difference.

Fix an integer \(m\). Construct two triangular sequences that equal \(Q_\delta\) at coordinate \(m\) and \(P^{\star}\) at every other coordinate, labeling coordinate \(m\) by PT in the first and by SC in the second. Each is in \(\mathfrak L_U(P^{\star})\): after its exceptional coordinate it is identically \(P^{\star}\), so its QMD score and remainder are eventually zero, and every coordinate satisfies the fixed strict margins established above. Hence, at every sample size, the frozen class contains two admissibly labeled copies of the same observed law.

Let \(z_{g,t}=3\mathbf 1\{G=g\}\{Y_t-\mu_{g,t}\}\). At \(Q_\delta\), donor innovation laws are unchanged, so
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(z_{2,3})=\frac32,
 \qquad \operatorname{Var}(z_{3,3})=6.
 \tag{4}
\]
At \(P^{\star}\), the common score has final donor coefficients \((-1/2,-1/2)\). The PT extension freezes its center normal coefficient, while donor laws are unchanged, so its final donor coefficients remain \((-1/2,-1/2)\) at \(Q_\delta\). The SC normal uses only preperiod coordinates, whereas (2) makes the SC final donor coefficients \((-1/2-\delta,-1/2+\delta)\). Therefore, for
\[
 \Delta_\delta
 =\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(Q_\delta;\mathrm{PT},P^{\star})
 -\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(Q_\delta;\mathrm{SC},P^{\star}),
 \tag{5}
\]
the final-innovation component is \(\delta(z_{2,3}-z_{3,3})\). Every other component uses distinct group-period innovations and is orthogonal to this one. Consequently,
\[
 E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta^2]
 \ge\delta^2\left(\frac32+6\right)
 =\frac{15}{2}\delta^2>0.
 \tag{6}
\]
Both chart scores are mean zero, so \(E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta]=0\).

Suppose one estimator had both chart expansions uniformly over the frozen class. Couple the two sequences at sample size \(m\) through the same iid sample from \(Q_\delta\). The causal target is the same under the two labels because \(Q_\delta\in\mathcal M_I\). Subtracting the two asserted uniform expansions would give
\[
 S_m=m^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^m\Delta_\delta(O_i)=o_{Q_\delta}(1).
 \tag{7}
\]
By independent sampling and (6),
\[
 E_{Q_\delta}[S_m^2]=E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta^2]
 \ge\frac{15}{2}\delta^2.
 \tag{8}
\]
Because \(\Delta_\delta\) is a bounded linear combination of finitely many Rademacher innovations,
\[
 E_{Q_\delta}[S_m^4]
 =m^{-1}E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta^4]
 +3(1-m^{-1})E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta^2]^2
 \tag{9}
\]
is uniformly bounded. Hence \((S_m^2)\) is uniformly integrable. Convergence in probability in (7) would imply \(E_{Q_\delta}[S_m^2]\to0\), contradicting (8). Thus no estimator has both chart expansions uniformly over \(\mathfrak L_U(P^{\star})\). Since asymptotic linearity is a necessary conjunct of the requested one-step, variance-consistency, and multiplier-coverage result, the complete affirmative result is false. The argument proves no positive continuation theorem on any redesigned sequence class.
